description: Selected exact provider output from October 25 Gaterr planning attempts. These excerpts omit requests and authentication; they are regression inputs, not accepted contracts.

captured_response.title: Install protected macOS service and authenticated IPC
captured_response.objective: Establish the real privilege boundary on macOS: a signed native daemon, root-owned installation and state, a dedicated unprivileged worker account, authenticated IPC with OS-derived peer UID, and a sandboxed worker that can run shell/Python/Make children without access to developer files or controller state. Signing and execution of repository commands remain disabled.
scope: Build signed native executables, root-owned installation/state paths, a system launch daemon, and the _powdrrattest worker identity.
Implement bounded IPC with OS-derived peer UID, profile ownership checks, and strict administrative/ordinary endpoint separation.
Implement the App Sandbox bootstrap for the worker and its children, with real macOS integration tests.
implementation_steps: Create the native daemon skeleton with Package.swift, launch daemon plist, root-owned installation paths under /Library/Application Support/PowdrrAttest/, and the _powdrrattest worker account; add health IPC with OS-derived peer UID checks.

Implement bounded IPC with protocol version 1, typed fields, caller-owned run IDs, and strict separation between ordinary run methods and administrative operations; add tests proving JSON fields cannot impersonate another user.

Implement the App Sandbox bootstrap for the worker and its children using Apple's supported sandbox inheritance mechanism; add real macOS integration tests proving the worker and its shell/Python/Make children can use their job container and network but cannot read developer-home fixtures, controller files, or an agent-controlled Python installation.

Add launch/library constraints and prevent user-owned dynamic dependencies; implement safe installation, upgrade, health, and explicit uninstall behavior with no automatic sudo invocation from run; add tests for caller-controlled paths and symlinks.
acceptance_criteria: 03-AC1: An ordinary enrolled developer UID can call health; a different unprovisioned UID and the worker UID cannot access profile operations.
03-AC2: Requests cannot impersonate another user by changing JSON fields.
03-AC3: Ordinary developer processes cannot modify the executable, daemon definition, profile state, socket parent directory, or future key directory.
03-AC4: PATH, Python packages, loader variables, caller cwd, and a repository executable named like the provider do not alter daemon code or dependencies.
03-AC5: Caller-controlled paths/symlinks cannot make installation or IPC write outside the fixed state locations.

captured_response.title: Define attestation schemas and shared fixtures
captured_response.objective: Freeze the protocol contracts and cross-language fixtures that every later component depends on.
scope: Create versioned JSON schemas for policy, attestors registry, predicate, and IPC.
Implement strict policy and registry parsers in Swift and Python with duplicate-key and resource-limit enforcement.
Add golden fixtures for DSSE statements, PAE bytes, keys, signatures, snapshot digests, and configuration errors.
implementation_steps: Add JSON schemas under attestation/schemas/ for policy-v1, attestors-v1, predicate-v1, and ipc-v1, encoding the field shapes and constraints from sections 4, 7, and 8.

Implement strict YAML parsers in Swift (using Yams with event auditing) and Python (using PyYAML with a custom loader) that reject duplicate keys, aliases, anchors, custom tags, unknown fields, and enforce size/step limits.
Implement raw-blob SHA-256 hashing, key fingerprint computation, snapshot record encoding, and step-definition digest computation in both languages, with unit tests.

Add fixture generators and golden files under attestation/fixtures/ covering valid and invalid policies, registries, snapshot digests, DSSE PAE bytes, and signed statements; wire them into attestation/scripts/verify-all.sh.
acceptance_criteria: 01-AC1: The sample Make and shell policies parse identically in Swift and Python; exact byte digests and ordered IDs match the frozen fixtures.
01-AC2: Every forbidden schema condition in section 4 has a rejecting fixture exercised by both implementations, including duplicate YAML keys and aliases.
01-AC3: Two fixtures with different YAML formatting have different raw policy digests even when their parsed meaning matches.
01-AC4: Snapshot digest fixtures cover ordinary files, executable files, symlinks, empty files, non-ASCII paths, and differing sort orders.
01-AC5: Unknown protocol/schema versions, floats in integer fields, oversized inputs, malformed dates, and key/fingerprint mismatches fail explicitly.

name: CI

  pull_request:

    branches: [main]
